description: Field mapping between MT940 (Customer Statement Message) and camt.053.001.10 (BankToCustomerStatementV10). MT940 is used by financial institutions to provide detailed account statement information with opening/closing balances and transaction entries. camt.053 is the ISO 20022 XML equivalent for bank-to-customer account statements.
mapping_notes: MT940 uses SWIFT character set (ASCII-based), while camt.053 supports full Unicode. Character set conversion may be required.
MT940 field lengths are generally shorter than camt.053 equivalents. MT to MX translation is usually lossless, but MX to MT may require truncation.
MT940 uses comma as decimal separator (e.g., 12345,67), while camt.053 uses period (e.g., 12345.67)
MT940 field 61 (Statement Line) can repeat multiple times, mapping to multiple Ntry (Entry) elements in camt.053
MT940 field 86 (Information to Account Owner) provides additional details for the preceding field 61, mapping to Ntry/NtryDtls/TxDtls or Ntry/AddtlNtryInf
Balance field codes in camt.053 use BalTp/CdOrPrtry/Cd: OPBD (opening booked), CLBD (closing booked), CLAV (closing available), FWAV (forward available)
MT940 balance types (60F/60M/62F/62M) map to camt.053 Bal elements with different BalTp codes and Tp/CdOrPrtry values: OPBD for opening, CLBD for closing
Field 61 D/C marks map to camt.053 CdtDbtInd: C->CRDT (credit), D->DBIT (debit), RC->CRDT with reversal indicator, RD->DBIT with reversal indicator
MT940 transaction type codes (field 61 position after amount) use SWIFT Bank Transaction Codes (e.g., NCHK, NTRF) which should be preserved in camt.053 Prtry/Tp
Date conversion: MT940 uses YYMMDD format, camt.053 uses ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD format with century inference (YY >= 50 -> 19YY, YY < 50 -> 20YY)

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 20 (Statement Reference) maps to Statement Identification. This is the unique reference assigned by the account servicing institution for the statement.
mappings.notes: Both formats use max 35 chars. MT940 field 20 is max 16 chars, so no truncation needed for MT->MX. MX->MT may require truncation if > 16 chars.
mappings.truncation_rule: If MX Stmt/Id > 16 chars, truncate to 16 chars for MT field 20

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 25 account number maps to Statement Account Identification. If account matches IBAN format (starts with 2-letter country code + 2 check digits), use Acct/Id/IBAN element; otherwise use Acct/Id/Othr/Id.
mappings.notes: Validate account format to determine IBAN vs other account number. Field 25 max 35 chars matches MX limits.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 25 account number maps to IBAN element if the account matches IBAN format. Validate using country code check and Mod-97 algorithm.
mappings.notes: IBAN validation: starts with 2-letter ISO 3166 country code + 2 check digits, passes Mod-97 validation. If valid, use IBAN element; otherwise use Othr/Id.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 25P format is BIC/Account. The account portion (after /) maps to Acct/Id/IBAN or Othr/Id based on format validation. The BIC portion maps to Stmt/Acct/Svcr/FinInstnId/BICFI.
mappings.notes: Field 25P is alternative to field 25. Parse: extract BIC (before /), extract account (after /). Validate account for IBAN format.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 25P BIC component (before /) maps to Account Servicer Financial Institution BIC. This identifies the institution holding the account.
mappings.notes: Extract BIC from field 25P by taking characters before the / separator. BIC is 8 or 11 characters.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 28C statement number (before optional /) maps to Legal Sequence Number. This is the sequential statement number.
mappings.notes: Field 28C format: StatementNumber[/SequenceNumber]. Extract first part (before /) for LglSeqNb. Second part (after /) is page/sequence within statement.

examples.notes: Statement 235, page 1 - page number goes to ElctrncSeqNb

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 28C sequence number (after /) maps to Electronic Sequence Number. This represents the page or sequence number within the statement.
mappings.notes: Extract second part of field 28C (after /) if present. If field 28C has no /, this element is omitted in MX.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60F maps to a Balance element with Type Code 'OPBD' (Opening Booked). The 'F' option indicates this is the final/first opening balance of the day.
mappings.notes: Create Bal element with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='OPBD' and Tp/SubTp/Prtry='FINAL' to indicate final opening balance. Either 60F or 60M present, not both.

examples.mx_value: Bal with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='OPBD', CdtDbtInd='CRDT', Dt/Dt='2026-02-10', Amt Ccy='EUR'>12345.67
examples.notes: Credit opening balance of EUR 12,345.67 on 2026-02-10

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60F first character (D/C mark) maps to Credit/Debit Indicator. C = CRDT (credit balance), D = DBIT (debit balance).
mappings.notes: Extract first character: C->CRDT, D->DBIT. Credit balance is positive, debit balance is negative/overdrawn.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60F date component (positions 2-7, YYMMDD) maps to Balance Date. Convert YYMMDD to ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD with century inference.
MT940 field 60F currency (positions 8-10) and amount (positions 11+) map to Balance Amount. Currency becomes Ccy attribute, amount value converted from comma to period decimal separator.
mappings.notes: Extract currency code (3 letters) and amount. Convert comma decimal separator to period. Currency is ISO 4217 code.

examples.notes: Extract EUR and 12345,67, convert to period decimal

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60M maps to a Balance element with Type Code 'OPBD' (Opening Booked). The 'M' option indicates this is an intermediate opening balance (not the first statement of the day).
mappings.notes: Create Bal element with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='OPBD' and Tp/SubTp/Prtry='INTERIM' to distinguish from 60F. Either 60F or 60M present, not both.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60M first character (D/C mark) maps to Credit/Debit Indicator. Same as 60F.
mappings.notes: C = CRDT, D = DBIT. Intermediate balance D/C indicator parsing is identical to final balance.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60M date component maps to Balance Date. Same format conversion as 60F.
mappings.notes: Convert YYMMDD to YYYY-MM-DD with century inference.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 60M currency and amount map to Balance Amount. Same format conversion as 60F.
mappings.notes: Extract currency and amount, convert comma to period decimal separator.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 (Statement Line) maps to an Entry (Ntry) element in camt.053. Each field 61 creates one Ntry. Field 61 has complex structure with 9 subfields that map to various Ntry subelements.
mappings.notes: Field 61 is repeating and complex. Parse all subfields: value date, entry date, D/C mark, funds code, amount, transaction type, customer reference, bank reference, supplementary details. Each subfield maps to specific Ntry elements.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 value date (positions 1-6, YYMMDD) maps to Entry Value Date. This is the date on which the entry is valued (funds available/debited).
mappings.notes: Convert YYMMDD to YYYY-MM-DD format with century inference. Value date is when funds become available (credit) or are debited.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 entry date (positions 7-10, MMDD, optional) maps to Entry Booking Date. If entry date is omitted in field 61, it equals the value date. Combine entry date MMDD with year from value date.
mappings.notes: Entry date is optional (MMDD format). If present, combine with year from value date. If omitted, BookgDt equals ValDt.

examples.notes: Entry date 0211 (Feb 11) with year 2026 from value date

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 D/C mark maps to Entry Credit/Debit Indicator. Lookup: C->CRDT, D->DBIT, RC->CRDT (reversal credit), RD->DBIT (reversal debit).
mappings.notes: D/C mark is mandatory. RC and RD indicate reversals. For reversals, set CdtDbtInd and also set Sts/Cd to 'RJCT' or use RvslInd.

examples.notes: Reversal of credit - set Rvsl element

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 funds code (optional third character after D/C mark) maps to Entry Status. Omitted or blank -> BOOK (booked), D -> PDNG (pending - funds on hold).
mappings.notes: Funds code is optional. Most entries are booked (omitted funds code). 'D' indicates funds pending/held. MX Sts element uses codes: BOOK, PDNG, INFO, etc.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 amount (after funds code, format: up to 15 digits with comma decimal) maps to Entry Amount. The currency is inherited from the balance fields (60F/60M), not specified in field 61.
mappings.notes: Convert comma decimal separator to period. Currency comes from statement currency (balance fields), so Amt Ccy attribute uses statement currency. Amount is unsigned (sign indicated by D/C mark).

examples.notes: Extract 1500,00, convert to 1500.00, currency from statement context

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 transaction type code (4 characters: 1 letter + 3 alphanumeric) maps to Bank Transaction Code Proprietary Code. Format: N=SWIFT codes, F=non-SWIFT codes, followed by 3-char type (e.g., NCHK=check, NTRF=transfer, NSTD=standing order, NDDT=direct debit).
mappings.notes: Preserve the full 4-character transaction type code. First char indicates SWIFT (N) or non-SWIFT (F). SWIFT bank transaction codes provide standardized type classification.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 customer reference (up to 16 chars after transaction type) maps to Transaction Details Account Servicer Reference. This is the reference for the account owner.
mappings.notes: Extract customer reference from field 61. Max 16 chars. This is the reference the customer sees on their statement.
mappings.truncation_rule: MX AcctSvcrRef max 35 chars, MT field 61 customer reference max 16 chars. No truncation needed MT->MX.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 bank reference (optional, preceded by //, up to 16 chars after //) maps to Entry Reference. This is the bank's internal reference for the entry.
mappings.notes: Bank reference is optional in field 61. If present, extract after // delimiter (remove //). Max 16 chars in MT, max 35 in MX.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 61 supplementary details (optional continuation line, up to 34 chars) maps to Additional Entry Information. This provides extra details about the transaction.
mappings.notes: Supplementary details appear on a continuation line in field 61 (after CRLF). Max 34 chars. Map to AddtlNtryInf for free-text additional info.
mappings.truncation_rule: MX AddtlNtryInf max 500 chars, MT field 61 supplementary details max 34 chars. No truncation needed MT->MX.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 86 (up to 6 lines of 65 chars, max 390 chars) maps to Transaction Details Remittance Information Unstructured. Field 86 follows field 61 and provides additional information about the transaction (payer/payee name, remittance info, etc.).
mappings.notes: Field 86 can be unstructured free text or structured with subfield codes (?20, ?21-?29, ?30, ?32, ?60, etc.). If unstructured, map entire content to RmtInf/Ustrd. If structured, parse subfields and map to appropriate elements (Dbtr/Nm for ?32, Cdtr/Nm for ?60, etc.).
mappings.truncation_rule: MX RmtInf/Ustrd max 140 chars per line, multiple lines allowed. MT field 86 max 390 chars total (6 lines x 65 chars). May need to split or truncate.

mappings.transform_details: If MT940 field 86 contains structured subfield codes, parse and map to Related Parties elements. Common codes: ?30 (sender BIC), ?32 (sender name), ?33 (sender address), ?60 (beneficiary BIC), ?62 (beneficiary name), ?63 (beneficiary address). Map ?32/?33 to Dbtr, ?62/?63 to Cdtr.
mappings.notes: Field 86 structured format is bank-proprietary. Common subfield codes start with ?NN. If structured format detected, parse subfields and populate RltdPties (Dbtr, Cdtr, etc.). If unstructured, use RmtInf/Ustrd instead.

mappings.transform_details: If field 86 content doesn't fit cleanly into RmtInf or RltdPties, or if it contains narrative description (?20-?29 codes), map to Additional Entry Information as overflow.
mappings.notes: Field 86 ?20-?29 codes typically contain transaction description/narrative. Map to AddtlNtryInf for supplementary free-text info.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62F maps to a Balance element with Type Code 'CLBD' (Closing Booked). The 'F' option indicates this is the final closing balance of the statement period.
mappings.notes: Create Bal element with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='CLBD' and Tp/SubTp/Prtry='FINAL'. Either 62F or 62M present, not both. Closing balance is mandatory.

examples.mx_value: Bal with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='CLBD', CdtDbtInd='CRDT', Dt/Dt='2026-02-10', Amt Ccy='EUR'>15845.67

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62F first character (D/C mark) maps to Credit/Debit Indicator. Same as opening balance.
mappings.notes: C = CRDT, D = DBIT. Closing balance D/C indicator parsing is identical to opening balance.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62F date component maps to Balance Date. Same format conversion as opening balance.
mappings.notes: Convert YYMMDD to YYYY-MM-DD with century inference. Closing balance date is typically the statement end date.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62F currency and amount map to Balance Amount. Same format conversion as opening balance.
mappings.notes: Extract currency and amount, convert comma to period decimal separator.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62M maps to a Balance element with Type Code 'CLBD' (Closing Booked). The 'M' option indicates this is an intermediate closing balance (not the final statement of the day).
mappings.notes: Create Bal element with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='CLBD' and Tp/SubTp/Prtry='INTERIM'. Either 62F or 62M present, not both.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62M first character (D/C mark) maps to Credit/Debit Indicator. Same as 62F.
mappings.notes: C = CRDT, D = DBIT.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62M date component maps to Balance Date. Same format conversion as 62F.
mappings.notes: Convert YYMMDD to YYYY-MM-DD with century inference.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 62M currency and amount map to Balance Amount. Same format conversion as 62F.
mappings.notes: Extract currency and amount, convert comma to period decimal separator.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 64 maps to a Balance element with Type Code 'CLAV' (Closing Available). This is the available balance after deducting holds/reserves from the booked balance.
mappings.notes: Create Bal element with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='CLAV'. Available balance shows funds actually available for use, which may differ from booked balance due to holds.

examples.mx_value: Bal with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='CLAV', CdtDbtInd='CRDT', Dt/Dt='2026-02-10', Amt Ccy='EUR'>14500.00
examples.notes: Available balance may be less than closing booked balance due to holds

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 64 first character (D/C mark) maps to Credit/Debit Indicator. Same as other balance fields.
mappings.notes: C = CRDT, D = DBIT.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 64 date component maps to Balance Date. Same format conversion as other balance fields.
mappings.notes: Convert YYMMDD to YYYY-MM-DD. Available balance date is typically same as closing balance date.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 64 currency and amount map to Balance Amount. Same format conversion as other balance fields.
mappings.notes: Extract currency and amount, convert comma to period decimal separator.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 65 maps to a Balance element with Type Code 'FWAV' (Forward Available). This shows projected available balance on a future date considering pending transactions.
mappings.notes: Create Bal element with Tp/CdOrPrtry/Cd='FWAV'. Field 65 can repeat for multiple future dates, creating multiple Bal elements. Each occurrence represents projected balance for different future date.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 65 first character (D/C mark) maps to Credit/Debit Indicator. Same as other balance fields.
mappings.notes: C = CRDT, D = DBIT. Forward available balance can be credit or debit.

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 65 date component maps to Balance Date. This is the future date for which the available balance is projected. Can be multiple days in the future.
mappings.notes: Convert YYMMDD to YYYY-MM-DD. Forward available balance date is future date (after closing balance date).

mappings.transform_details: MT940 field 65 currency and amount map to Balance Amount. Same format conversion as other balance fields.
mappings.notes: Extract currency and amount, convert comma to period decimal separator. Projected balance considering pending debits/credits.

mt_only_fields.reason: MT940 field 28C combines statement number and page/sequence number in single field (format: StmtNb/SeqNb). camt.053 separates these into LglSeqNb and ElctrncSeqNb. When translating MX to MT, must combine both elements into field 28C with / delimiter.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Generate unique identifier (UUID or timestamp-based) at translation time. MT940 field 20 is statement reference, not message ID.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 has no message-level ID concept (only statement reference in field 20). camt.053 requires GrpHdr/MsgId for message identification.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Use current timestamp at translation time. MT940 has no message creation timestamp field.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 has no explicit message creation timestamp. camt.053 requires CreDtTm to indicate when the message was created.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Can be derived from account owner information or institutional configuration. Optional element, can be omitted.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 is sent from bank to customer but doesn't explicitly identify the recipient in the message content. Recipient is implicit from message routing.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Use closing balance date (field 62F/62M) as date component, combine with current time. Or use current timestamp.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 balance fields contain dates but no timestamp. camt.053 CreDtTm includes both date and time for when statement was created.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Use currency from balance fields (60F/60M/62F/62M). All balance fields must have same currency in MT940.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 doesn't have explicit account currency field. Currency is in each balance/transaction field. camt.053 has Acct/Ccy to specify account currency once.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Omit. MT940 field 61 represents individual transactions, not batches.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 statement lines (field 61) are individual transactions. camt.053 supports batch indicators in Btch element but MT940 has no equivalent.

mx_only_fields.default_strategy: Calculate from MT940 entries: count field 61 occurrences for TtlNtries, sum credit amounts for TtlCdtNtries/Sum, sum debit amounts for TtlDbtNtries/Sum. Optional element.
mx_only_fields.reason: MT940 doesn't provide summary totals of transactions. camt.053 TxsSummary can be derived by counting and summing all field 61 entries.

key_differences_from_payment_messages: MT940/camt.053 are account statement messages, not payment instructions. They report historical transactions rather than initiate new payments.
Field 61 (Statement Line) can repeat many times within a single MT940 message, representing all transactions during the statement period. Each field 61 maps to one camt.053 Ntry element.
Balance consistency is critical: closing balance must equal opening balance plus sum of credits minus sum of debits from all field 61 entries.
Field 86 (Information to Account Owner) provides additional details for each transaction but has no standardized structure. Banks use proprietary formats, making parsing challenging.
MT940 has no customer/debtor/creditor party identification fields like MT103. Party information comes from field 86 unstructured text if present.
Transaction type codes in field 61 use SWIFT Bank Transaction Codes (NCHK, NTRF, etc.) which are preserved in camt.053 BkTxCd/Prtry/Cd.
Statement can have multiple balance types: opening (60F/60M), closing (62F/62M), closing available (64), forward available (65). Each maps to camt.053 Bal element with different BalTp codes.
